could_not_do: DID NOT REACH D2 >= 0.35 (full pass) ON JOURNAL, SHEET OR LEVEL-UP — only escaped the < 0.15 hard fail. Measured at HEAD (this round's commit): journal 0.1805, sheet 0.1713, level-up 0.1855 — all comfortably clear the hard-fail floor, none reach the 0.35 bar. THE REASON, MEASURED NOT GUESSED: shrinking a box that mostly holds FLOWING TEXT (journal's chronicle) or FIXED-BUT-NUMEROUS rows (sheet/level-up's ten attributes) loses matter almost as fast as it loses area, because fewer characters/rows fit on the smaller page. Two data points on journal make this precise: 760x585 (my first pass) raised D2 only 0.1314->0.1448 for a 62.5% area cut, because the matter itself fell from 155,788px2 to ~64,378px2 in step. A box small enough to reach 0.35 at that matter would need to be roughly 184,000px2 (8.9% of frame) for journal alone, by extrapolation from the measured matter/area relationship — and at that size the two-column chronicle and the quest index cannot both fit without further redesign (not just a resize) or losing more visible entries per page than this round already does. RECOMMENDATION FOR THE NEXT ROUND: reaching 0.35 on these three needs a lever beyond box size — likely tighter leading (RI-UIX05 B3 permits down to 1.35, currently 1.46-1.48) combined with a further, more surgical box cut, or accepting these three at 'hard-fail-cleared, bar not met' as this item's real ceiling given the no-added-elements constraint.

Measured against the r3 baseline (`corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/T4-r3c/measure/measure-live-1920x1080.json`, same commit lineage — HEAD's blobs for these 4 files matched the r3 pin exactly at the start of this round, checked via `git rev-parse <pin>:<path>` vs `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`): journal 30 -> 23 (-7), container 49 -> 33 (-16). BOTH ARE PAGINATION, NOT REMOVED CONTENT: journal's 19 entries all fit on ONE page inside the old 780-tall box; a shorter box moves 7 of them to page 2 (still reachable, `page N of M` is drawn and page-turn is unchanged). Container's `CROWS` dropped 12 -> 4 (both sides still scroll past 4 exactly as they scrolled past 12 — `windowOf` + `extent`, unchanged); the 44-item carried list already needed scrolling at 12 rows and needs more of it at 4. NEITHER IS FILLER (the acceptance's stated concern is a RISING count; both of these fell), and I checked both are pagination rather than data loss before writing this, but the acceptance text says '+/-2' without a direction and I did not satisfy it on these two screens as literally written. This is the single biggest thing for the next critic to weigh: does a pagination-caused decrease count against the same guard a filler-caused increase does? I did not decide this myself — see `arbitration_questions` below.
